# Button

A control that commits an action on this screen.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Button examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-button--docs">Open Button in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Every action.

- **Use it when:** The press does something here: save, submit, delete, open a dialog, go to the next step.
- **Not when:** The press only takes people to another page, or flips a setting that should persist.

Instead:

- [Toggle](./toggle.md): An on or off setting that should persist as state.
- Link: Navigation to another page or section.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An icon with no label</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Icon button with a tooltip</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A bare icon</div></div><div class="cap">Experts learn icons; the tooltip covers the first uses.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Keyboard focus</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> button/focus-ring at border-width.focus</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Removing the outline</div></div><div class="cap">Keyboard users must always see where they are.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The action that completes the task</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button primary, one per view</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Two primaries side by side</div></div><div class="cap">One primary makes the committing action obvious.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An alternative or cancel</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button ghost</div></div><div class="cap">A ghost button has no edge, so next to a filled primary it reads as plain text and cancel gets lost. Secondary keeps a visible border, so people find it at once.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Delete or remove</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary, then confirm in a dialog with Button danger</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button primary as the first step</div></div><div class="cap">Deleting is rare and costly; a confirm step catches mistakes.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An action on one row or item</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Icon button, ghost, compact</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button secondary in every row</div></div><div class="cap">Rows repeat dozens of times; a quiet icon keeps the table readable.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Button looks the way it does because of 9 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Button, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-color-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many emphasis levels do actions need?</b><code>color.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Three</div><p>One primary per view; the rest step back.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: The one commit in a view.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Acting on the wrong record</div><p>Acting on the wrong row is the costly error.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: The one commit in a view.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: Alternatives and cancel next to the primary, and the first step of a delete.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: The confirm of a bulk delete. <section class="odv-trail" id="why-iconography-roles"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What do icons do?</b><code>iconography.roles</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Actions and status</div><p>Icons mark row actions and status.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>icon</b>: Known row and toolbar actions, always with a tooltip.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Input group: inline-start</code> <code>Empty: icon</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-motion-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How fast does feedback feel?</b><code>motion.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Fast</div><p>Fast feedback keeps up with experts.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>hover</b>: Fast feedback that confirms the pointer.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-people-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What accessibility level do we commit to?</b><code>people.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">AA</div><p>AA is the floor for an internal tool used by trained staff.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>focus</b>: Always visible: the focus ring at border-width.focus.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>disabled</b>: Only with a visible reason next to it.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>and 3 answers that follow from it: <b>A ratio, line heights in proportion</b>, <b>Three: color, icon and word</b>, <b>AA</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moving through the page or a dialog. | Tab lands on the button in a logical order. | The control is skipped because it used HTML disabled. |
| The button is focused and the person confirms. | Enter runs the same action as a click. | Enter only works on submit buttons. |
| The button is focused. | Space runs the same action as a click. | Space scrolls the page instead. |
| The button opened a dialog, menu or popover that just closed. | After the action closes a surface, focus returns to the button. | Focus dropped on the page body. |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The control has a name assistive tech can speak. Any button, especially an icon-only one.
- [ ] The focused control stays visible; color alone is not the cue. Keyboard or assistive-tech focus is on the button.
- [ ] Unavailable stays in the tab order and explains why. The action must not run, but focus must not jump away.
- [ ] A button that stays down exposes its pressed state. Pin, follow, or another sticky on or off on a button.
- [ ] A button that opens something exposes open or closed. The press reveals a menu, panel or more content.
- [ ] The hit area stays usable, including at a small size. Touch, pointer, or a compact toolbar button.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add button
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Button reads 32 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Button's tokens to change Button alone.
